title_zh: 研究：童年體型偏離平均與成年抑鬱焦慮風險較高，成年體重正常者風險無顯著差異（368,756 人）
title_en: Body size trajectories childhood to adulthood depression anxiety risk UK Biobank
summary_zh: 英國生物樣本庫（UK Biobank）前瞻性隊列研究，368,756 名 40–69 歲成人，入組時無抑鬱或焦慮診斷，追蹤中位逾 13 年。10 歲時自述體型偏瘦者，成年抑鬱風險高 9%、焦慮高 13%；偏胖者抑鬱高 19%、焦慮高 11%。成年體重是主導因素：超重者抑鬱高 18%，肥胖者抑鬱高 52%、焦慮高 15%；童年偏瘦至成年肥胖組風險最高（抑鬱高 73%、焦慮高 33%）。童年偏胖但成年體重正常者，風險與一直平均者無顯著差異；成年 BMI 解釋童年偏胖與成年抑鬱關聯的約 45%。
summary_en: A UK Biobank prospective cohort study followed 368,756 adults aged 40-69 with no depression or anxiety diagnosis at enrolment for a median of over 13 years. Recalling a thinner-than-average body size at age 10 was associated with 9% higher depression risk and 13% higher anxiety risk in adulthood; a plumper-than-average childhood size with 19% higher depression and 11% higher anxiety risk. Adult weight was the dominant factor: overweight adults had 18% higher depression risk, and adults with obesity 52% higher depression and 15% higher anxiety risk; the thinner-in-childhood to obese-in-adulthood group had the highest risks (depression +73%, anxiety +33%). Participants plumper in childhood but at normal weight as adults showed no statistically significant excess risk; adult BMI explained about 45% of the link between childhood plumpness and adult depression.
evidence_note: 前瞻性隊列研究（Journal of Affective Disorders，2026-11-05 刊出；DOI: 10.1016/j.jad.2026.122042；UK Biobank，n=368,756；期刊頁未能直接讀取，經 PsyPost 2026-11-05 報道及另外兩篇報道交叉核對數字）

ethics_flags.note: 與家長或個案談童年體型與體重時，避免把心理健康風險歸咎於體重或造成體重污名；宜聚焦健康行為與支持，而非單一數字。
refs: 評估與篩檢｜假陽性與標籤效應

caution: 觀察性研究，不能證明體重導致抑鬱焦慮；10 歲體型靠數十年後回憶，有回憶偏差；UK Biobank 以歐洲裔志願者為主，代表性有限；合併多種診斷編碼，未分抑鬱焦慮亞型；「風險無顯著差異」是組別比較，不等於個別人士減重必然消除風險；談體重時須避免體重污名。

新發個案：抑鬱 11,546 人、焦慮 15,780 人
10 歲自述偏瘦：抑鬱風險高 9%、焦慮高 13%；偏胖：抑鬱高 19%、焦慮高 11%
成年超重：抑鬱高 18%；肥胖：抑鬱高 52%、焦慮高 15%；抑鬱風險最低 BMI 約 23–24
童年偏瘦至成年肥胖組風險最高：抑鬱高 73%、焦慮高 33%
童年偏胖但成年體重正常者：風險與一直平均者無顯著差異；成年 BMI 解釋約 45% 童年偏胖與成年抑鬱的關聯
supervision_questions: 家長擔心孩子體型影響將來心理健康時，你會如何談這份證據，而不加重體重焦慮或把問題簡化為體重？

posts.title: Losing childhood weight by adulthood might erase later depression risks (PsyPost 報道；原刊 Journal of Affective Disorders；DOI: 10.1016/j.jad.2026.122042)
posts.content: PsyPost 報道 UK Biobank 隊列研究：童年至成年體型軌跡與抑鬱焦慮風險，含各組風險比與中介分析。

related.title_zh: 兒福聯盟調查：三成五國高中生有容貌焦慮，口罩成「第二張臉」
related.title_en: Taiwan survey: 35% of teens report appearance anxiety
related.summary_zh: 兒福聯盟問卷調查全臺一萬多名國高中生，35.4% 自陳有容貌焦慮，少女 48.7%、少男 20.6%；23.5% 每天超過一半時間戴口罩，37.2% 看到他人網路照片後曾覺得自己很醜，47.8% 曾被平台主動推播相關內容。高容貌焦慮組有 25.1% 嚴重情緒困擾、29.6% 有自殺意念；兒盟建議理解口罩背後的心理防衛、避免強摘口罩或批評外貌，並以「鏡子練習」建立自我接納。
related.summary_en: A Children's Welfare League survey of over 10,000 Taiwanese secondary students found 35.4% report appearance anxiety (girls 48.7%, boys 20.6%). Among high-anxiety students, 29.6% reported suicidal ideation; 47.8% said platforms pushed appearance-related content to them.

related.title_zh: 統合分析：青少年花在社交媒體的時間，與焦慮憂鬱關聯極弱（37 項研究）
related.title_en: Social media time and teen anxiety depression meta-analysis
related.summary_zh: 澳洲天主教大學團隊在《British Journal of Clinical Psychology》發表的系統性回顧，綜合 37 項縱貫與實驗研究、近 80,000 名 10 至 24 歲青少年。社交媒體使用時間與其後抑鬱症狀的合併相關係數 r=0.08（12 項研究），焦慮 r=0.093（5 項研究），合共解釋不足 1% 的症狀差異。效應不隨年齡、追蹤期或發表年份改變。作者認為，單靠限制使用時間，未必能解決青少年心理健康危機。
related.summary_en: An Australian Catholic University systematic review in the British Journal of Clinical Psychology pooled 37 longitudinal and experimental studies of nearly 80,000 young people aged 10-24. Time on social media correlated only very weakly with later symptoms: depression pooled r = .08 (12 studies), anxiety r = .093 (5 studies), together explaining under 1% of symptom variation. Effects did not vary by age, follow-up length or publication year. The authors conclude restricting time alone is unlikely to resolve the youth mental-health crisis.

related.title_zh: 正向童年經驗與成年早期心理健康的長期追蹤研究
related.title_en: Positive childhood experiences reduce risk of later mental illness: longitudinal cohort
related.summary_zh: 縱向追蹤研究（發表於 American Journal of Psychiatry，2026 年 10 月 14 日，doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.20260007）。正向童年經驗（PCE）分數每增加 1 分（最高 10 分），成年早期符合精神障礙準則的機會率下降約 11%。
related.summary_en: Longitudinal study published in the American Journal of Psychiatry on 14 October 2026 (doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.20260007). Each one-point increase in positive childhood experiences (PCE, up to 10) was associated with about 11% lower odds of meeting criteria for a psychiatric disorder in early adulthood, after adjusting for confounders.
